hypothesis: The neuron responds selectively to monochromatic, grayscale imagery characterized by prominent horizontal stratification, banding, or linear structures. The activating features consist of horizontal edges, ridges, creases, text lines, or distinct layers of varying luminance (e.g., layers of clouds, wood grain, shadow bands, or lines of text) that traverse the image width. The neuron is strictly tuned to achromatic scenes—composed of blacks, whites, and shades of gray—and is invariant to the specific object identity (ranging from digital interfaces and printed menus to natural cloudscapes, animal profiles, and textured spheres) and surface texture (smooth, grainy, or matte), provided the horizontal directionality and lack of color are preserved. The horizontal elements typically span 70–100% of the image width and vary in vertical thickness, often creating a stacked or layered composition with moderate to high luminance contrast.

natural.description: An abstract composition of smooth, curvaceous, monochromatic forms with a matte, porcelain-like texture occupies the view, characterized by fluid geometry and soft, diffuse lighting. Dominating the upper left region is a large, convex, bulbous volume that curves downward and inward, transitioning from a bright white highlight near the top to a soft gray shadow along its lower contour. Beneath this upper mass, a separate undulating surface sweeps across the lower half of the frame, dipping into a deep, concave valley in the bottom center where the shadows deepen to a dark charcoal gray, suggesting a recess or hollow. To the right of this central dip, the lower surface rises steeply into a vertical, rounded ridge that curves slightly inward towards the left, creating a layered depth as it seemingly passes behind the upper bulbous form. The interplay between the shapes creates a sinuous, Y-shaped crevice of negative space and shadow where the upper sphere, the bottom valley, and the right-hand ridge converge. The lighting is even and ambient, casting no sharp edges but defining the three-dimensional volume through gradual gradients of white to gray, emphasizing the seamless, continuous nature of the twisting topology.

The subject is dominated by dense, coarse fur that appears bright white across the central chest and neck area, illuminated by a light source seemingly positioned at the upper left. A long, tubular snout extends prominently into the upper-left quadrant, ending in a dark, rounded nose pad with visible nostrils. The fur on the snout is short and sleek, transitioning into longer, shaggier hair as it moves back towards the neck and body in the center and right sections. On the far right edge, a patch of dark, charcoal-grey fur creates a high-contrast boundary against the white neck, suggesting a distinct marking on the animal's shoulder or back. In the lower-left quadrant, beneath the snout, a forelimb is tucked tightly against the body; the texture here is shadowed, revealing the curved, pale shapes of claws that blend subtly with the surrounding fur. The lighting creates soft shadows under the jawline and within the folds of the tucked limb, giving the form volume and depth, while the background remains a solid, indistinguishable black.
